personal.name: Francesco Done'
personal.title: Senior Frontend Engineer & Software Architect
personal.tagline: Building scalable platforms, guiding engineering teams, and turning complex systems into reliable user experiences.
personal.bio: From London to Munich — building the web, one city at a time.
autobiography: I grew up in Venice. If you have ever been there you know that nothing is laid out in a straight line, and I think that stuck with me. When I was eighteen I left for London. It was my very first time living outside Italy, and honestly I had no idea what I was doing. But that is exactly why it mattered. I came back with this feeling that I needed to keep going, keep seeing new places, keep figuring things out. So I did. I studied computer science in Padua, spent a semester in Copenhagen, and finished a master's in Milan. Each city taught me something different, but the thread was always the same: I wanted to understand how things work and how to build them better.

Then I moved to Germany, first to Düsseldorf and then to Munich. Living there changed the way I think about work. I learned to be structured, to be intentional, to care about doing things well rather than just doing a lot. But the part of me that grew up in Italy never went away either. That is where I learned how to listen, how to connect with people, and how to earn trust before trying to lead anything. There is one thing that ties all of this together, and it is the same whether I am at a desk or on a road. I have been running since I was a kid, and when I ran my first marathon in under three hours I realised the mindset that got me there was the exact same one I bring to work: show up every day, do not skip the boring parts, and trust that small consistent effort adds up to something big. That same approach is what led to being recognised with an Impact Award at work. It was not one flashy thing. It was months of showing up, pushing through the hard stretches, and caring about the outcome more than the credit. Between those two sides of my life I went from writing my first lines of code to designing architecture for large platforms. I speak four languages, and I still get excited every time I sit down to solve a problem I have not seen before.

journey.title: Web Developer Intern
journey.description: First professional experience abroad. Building websites for real clients, learning the craft of clean markup, and discovering that the web is built by people, not magic.

highlights: I was eighteen and had never lived outside Italy. That summer I built and maintained websites for real clients at a small creative agency, got my first taste of version control and deployment workflows, and figured out how to live on my own in a city where nobody knew me. It was short, but it changed everything.

journey.title: BSc Computer Science
journey.description: Algorithms, data structures, and the fundamentals that shape how you think about problems forever. Focus on Software Engineering.

highlights: Graduated with 97/110, focused on Software Engineering. During the final year I did a summer internship at Capgemini, which gave me the first taste of working on real software inside a large organisation.

links.label: Soldino
links.description: A decentralized DApp for VAT-compliant micro-payments on Ethereum, built with React, Redux, Solidity smart contracts, and IPFS. Developed by an eight-person team following a full software engineering lifecycle with formal documentation.

links.label: Soldino Docs
links.description: Complete project documentation including requirements analysis, technology assessment, design specification, and user/developer manuals produced for the Software Engineering course.

journey.title: Software Engineer
journey.description: A three-month software engineering internship in a large consulting environment, applying university foundations in a professional team.

highlights: A three-month internship during my bachelor's where I got to work on-site with a professional consulting team in Marcon, just outside Venice. It was my first real look at how software gets built inside a large organisation, and it made the theory from university feel a lot more concrete.

journey.title: MSc Computer Science
journey.description: Diving deep into Artificial Intelligence, AGI, and Human-Computer Interaction. A thesis that bridged neuroscience with reinforcement learning.

highlights: Graduated with 106/110, specialising in Artificial Intelligence with foundations in AGI and Human-Computer Interaction. Spent a semester on Erasmus exchange at the University of Copenhagen, and worked part-time as a Scrum Master and Software Engineer at IT Cube Consulting during the final year.

papers.label: Analysis of recurrent models of visual attention with reinforcement learning
papers.description: Master thesis bridging neuroscience with reinforcement learning, exploring how recurrent attention models learn to focus on relevant visual features.

journey.title: Erasmus Exchange
journey.description: A semester in Scandinavia to broaden perspectives. Software Engineering and AI in a new academic culture, sharpening both technical and cross-cultural skills.

highlights: Focused on Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, collaborating with international teams on research projects. Finished with an exam average of 12/12. It was a completely different academic culture, and working across backgrounds and perspectives sharpened both my technical and communication skills.

links.label: Question Answering system
links.description: A neural question answering system built with PyTorch as part of the NLP coursework.

links.label: Local-Volatility Calibration
links.description: Parallelizing volatility calibration on CPU (OpenMP) and GPU (CUDA) using the Crank-Nicolson finite difference method. The GPU version achieved over 30x speedup on large datasets.

links.label: Programming Massively Parallel Hardware
links.description: Covering GPU programming patterns, parallel scan, reduction, and optimisation techniques in CUDA and Futhark.

links.label: Vision and Image Processing
links.description: Five assignments spanning linear algebra for images, filtering and edge detection, photometric stereo, content-based image retrieval, and segmentation.

links.label: Collaborative Computing
links.description: Course report on collaborative computing models, exploring distributed systems and cooperative problem-solving strategies.

journey.title: Software Engineer
journey.description: Full-stack consulting across two client projects, growing from software engineer to project manager and Scrum Master.

highlights: I joined while finishing my master's and was placed on ITSentinel, a Windows Service agent that silently monitors machines, reporting on services, events, drives, and antivirus status every two minutes to a central dashboard built with Java, Spring Boot, and React. I started as a developer and grew into the project manager role, coordinating a four-person team and owning delivery end-to-end. The project ran on Agile Scrum, and the experience of shipping a real product for a paying client while juggling university gave me the pace and discipline I still carry.

journey.title: Frontend Engineer
journey.description: Moving to Germany and diving into enterprise-scale frontend development. Building digital experiences and growing into a confident engineer in an international team.

highlights: My first full-time role in Germany and my real entry into enterprise frontend. I worked in a hybrid international team building digital experiences, earned an Adobe Analytics Developer Professional certification along the way, and started to feel at home in the kind of large-scale, multi-team environment I would later grow into.

journey.title: Senior Frontend Engineer & Software Architect
journey.description: Architecting the digital showroom for Mercedes-Benz. Designing scalable BFF architectures, leading micro-frontend migrations, pioneering AI-driven development, and receiving the Impact Award in 2024 and 2025.

highlights: This is where things came together. I designed a scalable Backend-for-Frontend architecture, led a micro-frontend migration involving over 40 developers across six teams, and introduced error budget policies that gave us a shared language between reliability and speed. I built out frontend monitoring with Datadog and Terraform so teams could run on-call duty with confidence, cut bundle size by more than 80 percent, brought CLS down to nearly zero in an AEM environment, and led the SSR integration for Vue 3. More recently I have been designing AI agents with an AG-UI interface for the digital showroom and architecting a Generative Engine Optimization pipeline to make vehicles discoverable across LLMs. Along the way I received the Impact Award in both 2024 and 2025, which honestly meant a lot because it came from the same place as everything else I care about: showing up, doing the work, and making things better than I found them.
